about:
Missouri Basin Materials operates from Bismarck, North Dakota, serving as a concrete material supplier across the Midwest. The company provides rebar fabrication, anchor bolts, safety equipment, and a range of construction accessories to projects throughout North Dakota, Montana, Wyoming, and South Dakota.

The business combines a fabrication shop for reinforcing steel with a supply operation that stocks products from vendors such as Five Star Products, Newark Paperboard Products, Paragon Products, Polyguard Products, and various void form and forming systems. Its estimating department prepares quotes for projects ranging from ring wall foundations to water treatment plants, and the shop emphasizes quick turnaround on rebar fabrication and shop drawings.

Customers include general contractors, municipal agencies, and industrial builders working on infrastructure, commercial, and water treatment projects in the Upper Midwest. The company has supplied materials for ring wall foundations, water treatment plants, and other concrete-intensive structures across its service territory.

Missouri Basin Materials positions itself as a single-source provider for concrete-related materials, highlighting rapid rebar fabrication and shop drawing delivery as a key differentiator for contractors facing tight bid schedules.

name: Mitas Electronics
old_description: Mitas Electronics combines miniature high-speed interconnect experience, precision manufacturing discipline, and future-facing transport architecture work to support more predictable physical data movement as systems scale.
about:
Mitas Electronics is based in Round Rock, Texas, and has accumulated over 17 years of operating history. The company was founded as an engineering-led organization focused on miniature high-speed interconnect systems, though the exact founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed.

The company designs and manufactures miniature high-speed cable assemblies and interconnect systems, providing interconnect engineering, manufacturing coordination, and technical support. Its capabilities span application review, mechanical fit, signal-path awareness, DFMA, supply chain management, process documentation, and quality-focused execution across manufacturing partners. Mitas also produces technical binders—engineering resources that include connector specifications, application guides, and manufacturability considerations for cable assembly designers. To date, the company reports shipping more than 4 million cables, serving over 500 customers, and delivering more than 2,200 tailored solutions.

Mitas serves customers in high-speed data transport, electronic systems, and computing infrastructure markets. Its technical binders and interactive viewers support established interconnect families such as QSFP-DD, CABLINE-CA II, and CABLINE-VS II, catering to engineers who need dimensional context, inspection guidance, and application-specific selection support.

The company differentiates itself through a transport-physics mindset and a developing architecture called GFx™, aiming to make physical data movement more predictable as computing architectures scale. Mitas emphasizes disciplined manufacturing coordination, defined inspection steps, traceability practices, and continual improvement driven by manufacturing feedback.

name: Mitchell Furniture Systems Inc
old_description: As an innovator in wall mounted table and bench systems since the early 1950’s, Mitchell offers value without compromising its pledge for a safe and secure product that will provide decades of service.
about:
Mitchell Furniture Systems traces its roots to Milwaukee, Wisconsin, where William Mitchell founded the company in 1896 to produce dairy farming equipment such as automatic stalls and stanchions. The business expanded into steel products for parks and playgrounds before pivoting in the 1940s to folding leg tables, choral risers, and wall-mounted table and bench systems for cafeterias. Today the company operates manufacturing plants in Fredonia and Milwaukee, maintaining a “Made in America” commitment with seasoned metal fabricators and assemblers using both time-honored techniques and robotic welding.

The product line centers on wall-mounted table and bench systems (NPX and ST series), mobile tables with integrated seating (PorTables), fold-and-roll tables (Fold-N-Roll), convertible 3-in-1 ConverTables, adjustable-height folding tables (Saturna and Fold-O-Leg), and risers for stages and seating. Production combines steel frame fabrication, robotic welding, wood top machining, and final assembly. The company also offers a table-top replacement service for both its own and competitors’ tables.

Primary customers include K–12 school districts, universities, municipalities, churches, corporate offices, and conference centers. Historical markets encompassed dairy farming and municipal park systems. The company cites installations in cafeterias, fellowship halls, classrooms, lecture halls, and theaters as typical applications.

Mitchell emphasizes that its products are engineered for decades of service, noting that many risers sold in the late 1940s remain in use. The firm differentiates itself through domestic manufacturing, robotic welding for consistency, and a willingness to retrofit competitors’ tables with Mitchell tops.

name: Mitsubishi Electric US, Inc., Industrial Automation
old_description: Mitsubishi Electric US, Industrial Automation announces the launch of the GOT3000 Series HMI, the next generation of human-machine interfaces, to its existing lineup. GOT3000 delivers faster performance, enhanced security, and compatibility with prior GOT models. It delivers a practical path to modernization without the need for rip-and-replace upgrades.
about:
Mitsubishi Electric US, Inc., Industrial Automation is headquartered in Vernon Hills, Illinois. The division operates as part of Mitsubishi Electric Corporation, which celebrated its 100th anniversary in February 2021. The U.S. automation business supports customers across the Americas from a single facility that houses manufacturing, engineering, training, service, and warehousing functions.

The company designs and manufactures a broad range of factory automation equipment, including programmable logic controllers (MELSEC series), human-machine interfaces (GOT series), variable frequency drives (FREQROL series), AC servo systems (MELSERVO), industrial robots (MELFA and ASSISTA collaborative robots), CNC controllers, low-voltage power distribution products, laser processing machines, and electrical discharge machines. It also provides engineering software, network products, system integration, technical support, repair services, and training programs.

Its customers span mining, water and wastewater treatment, automotive, education, and general manufacturing. Concrete examples include DICISA in mining, Bertelkamp Automation for municipal water systems, Renault Group for e-motor production, Kettering University for hands-on automation education, and Usinage Précision Bilodeau for precision machining.

The division’s stated mission is to support industrial automation needs in the Americas by combining sales, marketing, service, engineering, and manufacturing resources in one location. It emphasizes rapid repair turnaround using custom parts, on-site training, and a culture of continuous improvement (Kaizen) that places it among the top five global patent filers. The e-F@ctory initiative leverages IoT and big data to create smart factory solutions.

about:

Its sales team brings over 100 years of combined connector experience, providing application consultation, connector inspections, and counterfeit prevention services. The company emphasizes same-day shipping capabilities for in-stock items and includes certification with each shipment under its ISO 9001:2015 quality system.

Mobile Electronics serves clients worldwide across aerospace, defense, and medical industries, with a strong presence in the avionics sector. Its customer base includes large manufacturing firms that rely on the distributor's ability to identify optimal interconnect solutions from project descriptions rather than part numbers alone.

The company attributes its competitive edge to the versatility and flexibility afforded by its small business structure, coupled with deep product knowledge. It highlights counterfeit prevention that exceeds industry standards and a commitment to rapid order fulfillment to prevent project delays.

name: Modular Components National
old_description: Modular Components National is a manufacturer of printed microwave circuit boards.
about:
Modular Components National was founded in 1981 in Forest Hill, Maryland. The company has operated from this location for over four decades, serving government and commercial RF customers.

The company manufactures printed microwave circuit boards, specializing in PTFE substrates and high-reliability, tight-tolerance circuitry for RF, microwave, and millimeter-wave applications. Its fabrication capabilities include single- and double-sided circuits (0.002″ to 0.250″ thick), metal-backed circuits with fusion bonding and post-fabrication attachment, and multilayer constructions using PTFE, mixed dielectrics, FR-4, and microwave laminates. Proprietary processes support embedded copper heat-sink cores, thermoclastic bond films such as FEP lamination, and laser routing for thin dielectrics with complex profiles. Materials sourced from Arlon, Rogers, and Taconic are used throughout.

MCN serves the defense, aerospace, telecommunications, and medical markets, as well as broader government and commercial RF sectors. Its sales representative network covers regions across the United States, Canada, and Israel.
